item.title: Loose protected stonework outside the property boundary, 26th August
item.description:
Along Broadway Road, there is a long boundary fence to Charingworth Court. Between that boundary the pavement side there is a long verge, until this year always cut once by GCC Highways for pedestrians. And at the end a length too vertical to mow, which was used to be trimmed by the GCC. I understand such land is only managed if there is a road safety reason. So, to address the large weeds, I have mowed the whole length. But at the town centre end, there's an angled "wall" of longstanding stones, to hold back the higher land. This short length is too steep for grass, and where the pavement is also narrower. The "wall" of large stones ensured that the pavement is passable safely. Over time, however, these stones have lost their mortar, and are becoming unsafe. Youngsters could be tempted to looking to climb up on them, which could result in an accident. Over the years, I have addressed the weeds that would otherwise force pedestrians into Broadway Road. But action is needed to set the stones with new mortar to avoid wanting to climb etc.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): B4632, Winchcombe, Winchcombe, Tewkesbury
Report on FixMyStreet
